text.p: Fake car wrecks, false claims for a stolen fishing boat and works of art and a couple who slipped up trying to rip off shops figured in Florida's Top Ten insurance scams last year, the state insurance department said Friday.

In Operation Big Broom, state investigators nabbed 63 suspects ranging from lawyers to chiropractors in the biggest single-day sweep against insurance fraud in Florida's history. The case involved phony medical claims, the department said in a statement.

Operation Money Box also dealt with phoney medical claims -- 3,000 in all. Investigators uncovered a scam involving dozens of suspects using fake companies to bilk more than 50 insurance companies out of $51 milllion.
And in Operation Smash and Grab, authorities broke a ring staging car wrecks to claim fake injuries.
State treasurer and insurance commissioner Bill Nelson said the department's fraud division made nearly 500 arrests last year, up 12 percent from last fiscal year.
Nelson told a conference of fraud investigators in Orlando that insurance scams cost each Florida family $1,500 a year.
"Anything we can do to combat this crime is good for consumers," he said. "They are the hidden victims in such crimes."

Among scams in the annual Top Ten unveiled by Nelson was the case of a former Miami police officer who reported his $200,000 luxury fishing boat "Done Deal" stolen. Investigators learned of arrangements to have it transported to Colombia and the Coastguard picked it up off Haiti. The owner was arrested.

A Santa Rosa county man was arrested after claiming benefits for work-site accidents that he said left him unable to work. Investigators on stake-out watched him swinging hammers, lifting beams and climbing ladders.
A Miami woman claimed $12,000 worth of works of art was stolen from her home in a burglary. She submitted receipts to the insurance company, but it turned out she had never purchased the art.

An Aventura condominium association put in a $2 million claim for damage done to patios and pool decks in 1992's Hurricane Andrew. The association directors were discovered to have removed from their files records showing the damage occurred before the storm hit.
One couple filed a series of slip-and-fall claims against more than 20 Florida stores, giving false names to shop staff.

And a Palm County man was jailed after his ex-wife refused to help him out in $20,000 scam over his Jaguar car. He reported it stolen and asked her to remove the vehicle from storage. She declined -- and investigators found he had changed the car's papers from joint ownership with the woman to solely owned by him.
